title: Steel racks on a semi-trailer
story: Five racks of steel posts held by chains and straps: they hold, but is the weight legal?
story_pt: Cinco racks de postes de aço presos com correntes e cintas: aguentam, mas o peso está dentro da lei?

truck.uncertain: no side rails visible; trailer may be extendable

units.uncertain: steel rack frame holding upright metal anodes or bars; closest type crate
rack count and exact positions uncertain

restraints.uncertain: a chain hangs on the rear rack; other lashings not visible from this angle
green items at rack bases may be straps or tensioners

violations.note: Upright bars stand well above the low headboard and could move forward.

analysis.summary: A flatbed semi-trailer carries about five steel racks of tall upright metal bars on its front two thirds, with only a few visible chain/strap lashings.

links.uncertain: steel rack frame holding upright metal anodes or bars; closest type crate
rack count and exact positions uncertain

findings.message: Axle group tractor carries 19.45 t; the legal limit is 17.0 t.

contran_945.message: Only straps, chains, blocking or mats secure the load.
Every lashed unit has lashings rated for at least twice its weight.
Each unit is secured with at least 4 lashing terminals.
Lashings are anchored to the truck's lashing points on the metal frame.
No room to travel along the truck, or diagonal devices hold the load.
Diagonal devices or blocking hold every unit forward and backward.
No cargo uses an open body's headboard as a stop.
Nothing above the headboard can slide forward over it.
